# 1 Maccabees Chapter 9 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 9 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_009_page_001.jpg

---

**1** When news reached Demetrius that Nicanor had been killed along with his army, he dispatched Bacchides and Alcimus back into Judea for a second campaign, this time with the army's elite right flank.

**2** They took the road toward Gilgal and set up camp against Mesaloth in Arbela, capturing the city and massacring many of its people.

**3** In the spring of 160 BCE, they moved their camp to the outskirts of Jerusalem.

**4** From there they marched to Berea — twenty thousand foot soldiers and two thousand cavalry.

**5** Judas had his camp at Elasa with three thousand chosen fighters.

**6** One look at the enemy's overwhelming numbers, and fear swept through the Jewish ranks. Men began slipping away from camp one by one until only eight hundred remained.

**7** Judas watched his army dissolve before his eyes. The battle was already closing in, and he had no time to rally them. His heart broke within him.

**8** Still, he summoned his courage and said to the men who stayed: "Up — let us go and meet them. We may yet be able to fight."

**9** His men urged him back: "We can't win this one. Let's retreat, save ourselves, and come back with more men. We're outnumbered now."

**10** Judas would not hear of it. "God forbid I should run from them. If our time has come, let us die like men, for the sake of our brothers. We will leave no one cause to question our honor."

**11** The Syrian army poured out of its camp and arrayed itself against them. The cavalry split into two wings. Slingers and archers took their places in the vanguard. The shock troops held the front line.

**12** Bacchides took command on the right flank. The phalanx advanced on both sides, trumpets sounding.

**13** Judas's men sounded their own trumpets. The ground shook with the noise of both armies colliding. They fought from dawn until dusk.

**14** Judas saw that Bacchides himself and the main strength of the Syrian army were concentrated on the right flank, and he threw everything he had against them.

**15** He broke the right wing and chased them all the way to the slopes of Azotus.

**16** But those on the left flank, seeing the right had caved, swung around and hit Judas and his men from behind.

**17** The fighting turned savage. Both sides suffered heavy casualties.

**18** Then Judas fell. The rest ran.

**19** Jonathan and Simon gathered their brother's body and carried him to Modein, burying him in the tomb of their ancestors.

**20** They wept over him. All Israel grieved deeply, mourning for many days. Their lament rang out:

**21** "How has the mighty warrior fallen — the man who saved Israel!"

**22** The full account of Judas's wars, his feats of courage, and his greatness was never written down, for there was simply too much to record.

**23** In the wake of Judas's death, lawbreakers crawled out of every corner of Israel. Evil men who had been in hiding came back into the open.

**24** A terrible famine struck the country that year, and the population, desperate for survival, began siding with the enemy.

**25** Bacchides deliberately handpicked traitors and installed them as governors across the land.

**26** They hunted down every known friend of Judas, dragged them before Bacchides, and Bacchides made them suffer.

**27** Israel had never known such oppression — not since the last prophet had gone silent.

**28** All the surviving companions of Judas came together and approached Jonathan:

**29** "Since your brother Judas died, there is no one who can lead us against our enemies — against Bacchides and against the men who hate our people.

**30** Today we are choosing you — you are our commander and our leader, to stand where he stood, and to fight our battles."

**31** Jonathan accepted the burden of leadership and stepped into his brother's role.

**32** Bacchides got word of it and immediately began plotting to kill him.

**33** Jonathan got wind of it first. He, his brother Simon, and all their men fled into the wilderness of Tekoa and camped by the pool of Asphar.

**34** Bacchides found out on the Sabbath and crossed the Jordan with his full army.

**35** Jonathan had already sent his brother John ahead as commander of the baggage train to negotiate with the Nabatean allies for storage of their equipment.

**36** But the sons of Jambri ambushed John on the way out of Medaba, seized him, and made off with everything he was carrying.

**37** Some time afterward, Jonathan and Simon received word that the sons of Jambri were throwing a lavish wedding feast — escorting the bride, a daughter of one of Canaan's most powerful nobles, from Nadabath with a great procession.

**38** They thought of John their brother. And they moved.

**39** They went up and took position on the hillside overlooking the road. Looking down, they saw a loud procession — loads of baggage, and then the groom arriving with friends and brothers, with drums and musicians and armed escorts.

**40** They burst from ambush and cut them down. Many died. The survivors scattered into the hills. The Jews took all the spoil.

**41** A wedding became a funeral. Music became weeping.

**42** Blood had been answered with blood. They withdrew to the marshes of the Jordan.

**43** When Bacchides got word, he came to the Jordan's bank that same Sabbath with a great army.

**44** Jonathan rallied his men: "This is not the time to hesitate — fight for your lives! Today is nothing like before.

**45** Look at our situation — enemy in front, enemy behind, the Jordan on both sides, swamp and thicket all around. Nowhere to run.

**46** Cry out to God — right now — and he will save you from their hands."

**47** Battle was joined. Jonathan lunged at Bacchides himself, but Bacchides dodged away.

**48** Jonathan and his men dove into the Jordan and swam to the far bank. The Syrians did not cross after them.

**49** Bacchides lost about one thousand men that day.

**50** He returned to Jerusalem and set about fortifying Judea with a string of strongholds: Jericho, Emmaus, Beth-horon, Bethel, Timnath, Pharathon, and Tephon — all reinforced with high walls, heavy gates, and iron bars.

**51** He stationed garrisons in each one to keep the pressure on Israel.

**52** Beth-zur, Gazara, and the Jerusalem citadel were also strengthened and stocked with troops and provisions.

**53** He took the sons of the leading families of Judea as hostages and locked them in the citadel under armed guard.

**54** In the spring of 159 BCE, the high priest Alcimus ordered the demolition of the inner court wall of the sanctuary — tearing down a structure that had been built by the prophets. Work began immediately.

**55** But as demolition started, Alcimus was suddenly struck down. His projects ground to a halt, his mouth was locked shut. He was paralyzed and could not speak a single word or manage his own household.

**56** And Alcimus died, in great suffering.

**57** With Alcimus dead, Bacchides returned to the king. Judea had two years of quiet.

**58** Then the traitors put their heads together: "Jonathan and his men are settled in and feel safe. Let us bring Bacchides back — he can wipe them all out in one night."

**59** They went and laid out the plan for Bacchides.

**60** He assembled a large army and sent secret letters to all his agents in Judea, ordering them to seize Jonathan and his companions. But the plot leaked.

**61** Jonathan and his men grabbed about fifty of the local ringleaders who had been behind the conspiracy and executed them.

**62** Then Jonathan, Simon, and their followers fell back to Bethbasi in the wilderness, rebuilt what had been torn down, and fortified it.

**63** Bacchides heard and mobilized his whole force, alerting all his contacts in Judea.

**64** He besieged Bethbasi and hammered at it for days, building siege equipment.

**65** Jonathan made a decision: he left Simon in charge of the city and slipped out into the countryside with a strike force.

**66** He hit Odomera and his brothers and the sons of Phaseron in their encampments, inflicting casualties, and pressing the attack.

**67** Meanwhile Simon led a sortie from the city and burned the siege machines.

**68** The combined pressure broke Bacchides. The campaign had cost him everything and gained him nothing.

**69** He turned his fury on the traitors who had talked him into the whole operation and executed many of them. Then he decided to go home.

**70** Jonathan heard about his change of heart and sent envoys to negotiate peace and secure the return of prisoners.

**71** Bacchides agreed readily, kept his word, and swore under oath that he would never again move against Jonathan as long as he lived.

**72** He released all the Jewish prisoners he had taken in Judea, turned around, and went back to Syria — and he never set foot in their land again.

**73** And the sword was quiet in Israel. Jonathan settled at Michmash and began governing the people, routing out every apostate from the land.
